policy.official: A league or club publication. Only these may ground a row in the verified master list (data/archive.json).
policy.partner: A free, keyless, publicly reachable hosted feed (ESPN's site endpoints). Useful for live game state, timestamps and leads. Never grounds a verified archive row on its own.
policy.unofficial: Public social or aggregator material (Mastodon, Google News RSS, CBS-style trackers, X/Instagram/Facebook/TikTok/Reddit). Leads and context only: never auto-published as a verified claim.
policy.rule: A lane may only ever be shown with its tier label. An unofficial or partner item is never presented as a verified in-game injury. Absence of a report never implies a player is healthy.

sources.name: Club injured-reserve news item
sources.what: A club story confirming two tight ends moving to injured reserve after one game.
sources.proves: Club confirmation of IR moves that the league roundup then reports.
sources.latency: Within a day of the game.

verification.method: Re-listed from the archive's citation set for the Kolar and Njoku rows; content is club-authored.

sources.notes: Note the reversal the next day (Kolar ultimately stayed off IR), which is why the registry records latency and edits rather than mere existence.

sources.name: Club game-day recap
sources.what: The club's own recap of a single game, including a plain sentence about who was lost during it.
sources.proves: A club statement placing an injury inside a specific game ('The Saints lost left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. in the third quarter with an ankle injury and cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. to a shoulder injury in the first half.').

verification.method: Fetched the page this session and read the sentence above verbatim; the URL shape is /game-day/{season}/reg-week{n}/{away}-vs-{home}/recap on the shared club platform.

sources.notes: scripts/schema.py now allowlists club /game-day/ paths so these recap URLs can ground an archive row.

sources.name: Club game report (per-club)
sources.what: A club's long-form game report, ending in a club-specific injury report section covering both sidelines.
sources.proves: In-game injuries for the reporting club and, unusually, its opponent in one page.
sources.latency: Same evening as the game (published Sept 20, 2026 at 7:07 PM).

verification.method: Content retrieved this session; the page's 'Jaguars injury report' section is where the club lists its in-game losses.

sources.notes: Prized shape for coverage gaps: one fetch can fill two teams. Listed as next-session mining work.

sources.name: Club in-game injury update pages
sources.org: NFL clubs (Seattle, Green Bay verified; pattern is per-club)
sources.what: A live page a club updates during its own game: 'RB Jadarian Price is questionable to return with a chest injury', 'NT Brandon Pili ... has been ruled out.'
sources.proves: In-game availability as the club announced it, with quote-ready sentences.
sources.latency: Best case for a static site: the page updates within minutes; discovery still depends on the collector noticing the URL.

verification.method: Content retrieved and read this session (search index of the Seattle page plus the already-published archive row that cites it); the companion postgame page https://www.seahawks.com/news/updates-on-sam-darnold-jadarian-price-other-seahawks-injuries was fetched in full ('running back Jadarian Price will be on the field after exiting Sunday's win in Arizona early due to a shoulder injury').

sources.notes: Only some clubs publish these pages. Discovery of the per-game URL is the open problem: the collector currently has no club-wide index for it. Flagged as next-session work.

sources.name: Club injury news item (per-club)
sources.what: A single club story dedicated to injury news: season-ending surgery, IR placements, return timelines.
sources.proves: A club's own confirmation of a season-ending or injured-reserve outcome for a named player.
sources.latency: Hours after the coach's press conference.

verification.method: Re-listed from the archive's citation set; multiple clubs publish this shape, e.g. azcardinals.com 'LaFleur: Will Johnson could be sidelined for season'.

sources.notes: Where the archive's 'out indefinitely' and 'miss the remainder of the season' language comes from.

sources.name: Club newsrooms (32 teams)
sources.what: Club-authored game recaps, in-game injury update pages, practice notes, press conferences and roster/IR announcements.
sources.proves: A club's own statement about its player. Clubs are the most detailed and usually the earliest in-game voice.
sources.latency: In-game update pages can be minutes after the play; recaps after the game.

verification.method: Fetched club pages this session across the platform shared by all 32 clubs (static.clubs.nfl.com assets): Seahawks, Patriots, Saints (see club-game-day-recap), plus club URLs already cited by archive rows (Packers, Cowboys, Jets, Colts, Cardinals, Chargers, Commanders, Broncos, Bills, Falcons, Browns, Eagles, Buccaneers, Jaguars, Seahawks, 49ers).

sources.notes: Hosts allowlisted in scripts/schema.py (all 32 newsroom domains) and mirrored in assets/app.js.

sources.name: Club game-day recap (per-club)

sources.name: Club practice notebook / injury notebook
sources.what: A club's weekly notebook: who is heading to injured reserve, who was held out, and what the coach said about the previous game.
sources.proves: A dated, club-authored follow-up that ties a player's absence back to the game he was hurt in.

verification.method: Already cited by archive rows and re-listed here; content is club-authored and the URL shape is stable per club.

sources.notes: The most efficient official follow-up source per club; titles are searchable.

sources.name: NFL.com news roundup (daily league updates)
sources.what: Per-club INJURIES/SIGNINGS/ROSTER CUTS blocks mixing practice participation with dated follow-ups (IR placements, coach comments, reported diagnoses).
sources.proves: A dated league-published follow-up (e.g. an IR placement or a coach quote) for a named player.
sources.latency: Daily, typically after practice; same-week follow-ups only.

verification.method: Fetched the Sept 16, Sept 18 and Sept 22, 2026 editions this session. Sept 16 carries practice statuses (e.g. 'Kitan Crawford suffered a mid-ankle sprain in Arizona's Week 1 win'); Sept 22 carries 'Jayden Reed (neck) is back in Green Bay after he stayed overnight in New Jersey after he exited Sunday's win over the Jets on a stretcher.'

sources.notes: Most bullets are practice/roster status, NOT in-game events. The collector will only promote a bullet that carries an explicit in-game anchor.

sources.name: NFL game-center JSON (api.nfl.com)
sources.what: Would be the league's own structured game-center payload (play-by-play and injuries).
sources.proves: Nothing at present: the endpoint refuses unauthenticated reads.

verification.method: Direct probe returned 'HTTP 401 Unauthorized / Error 54113 / Varnish cache server'.

sources.notes: This is why the project cannot claim an official NFL play-by-play feed. NFL.com player-facing pages are JavaScript-driven and expose no verified public play-by-play JSON. Do not describe any lane as 'official NFL play-by-play' until this returns data.

sources.name: NFL.com official injury report
sources.what: The league's weekly per-game practice/status report (Player | Position | Injury | Practice Status | Game Status).
sources.proves: Pregame practice participation and game designation only.
sources.latency: Weekly, published on the league's reporting schedule.

verification.method: Not re-probed in this session. The prior session's ledger recorded HTTP 200 with a Week 1 2026 title (probed 2026-09-10 from a GitHub Actions runner).

sources.notes: Deliberately excluded from in-game logic: it is a pregame report and conflating it with in-game status is the failure mode this project exists to avoid. A re-probe is scheduled for the next pass.

sources.latency: Published during or after the Sunday slate; the Week 1 edition carries a Sept 13, 2026 timestamp.

sources.name: ESPN injuries feed

sources.name: ESPN NFL Injury Status page

sources.latency: Minutes; comments carry a date but not a clock time.

sources.name: ESPN NFL news feed
sources.what: Headlines, descriptions, published/lastModified timestamps, team and athlete tags, and web links.
sources.proves: That ESPN published a story at a stated minute. Useful as a timestamped lead, not as a verified in-game fact.
sources.latency: Seconds to minutes after ESPN publishes.

sources.name: ESPN public scoreboard API

verification.method: Fetched this session: returned the 2026 season calendar and Week 3 with event 401872948 (Atlanta Falcons at Green Bay Packers, 2026-09-25T00:15Z, playByPlayAvailable false before kickoff).

sources.name: ESPN scoreboard header (fast lane)
sources.what: Small league-level payload: events with id, date, fullStatus (state/period/clock), competitors with scores and situation/playByPlayAvailable flags.

verification.method: Fetched this session with dates=20260920: returned event 401872933 (Carolina Panthers at Atlanta Falcons) with fullStatus {state: 'post', displayPeriod: '4th'}, competitors and playByPlayAvailable true.

sources.name: ESPN game summary incl. play-by-play
sources.what: Full game package: boxscore, drives/plays, leaders, header.
sources.proves: Game state and play text. This session could NOT verify that ESPN play text carries an injury vocabulary: the payload is very large (the 401872933 response paginates to 72 chunks) and the sibling cdn.espn.com play-by-play payload (75 chunks) mixes news with plays.
sources.latency: Seconds, but the payload size makes it unsuitable for frequent polling in a browser tab.

verification.method: Fetched ?event=401872933 (HTTP 200, boxscore and player sections present) and cdn.espn.com/core/nfl/playbyplay?xhr=1&gameId=401872932 (HTTP 200, 75 chunks, news objects interleaved).

sources.notes: Deliberately NOT used to claim injuries. The site states plainly that play-by-play injury detection is unproven here, and the vocabulary test is listed as next-session work. No code may describe this lane as 'official NFL play-by-play'.
